title: From polynomial-time randomized machines to verifiers
statement: Let $L$ be a language of bit strings that is decided by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with some running-time bound $c(n^d+1)$, where $c,d$ are natural numbers: for every input of length $n$, every choice string of that length causes the machine to halt within the bound, and the probability that its output is the correct membership bit is at least $2/3$. Then there is a Boolean randomized verifier whose deterministic acceptance and rejection relations are polynomial-time decidable and which, on each input $x$, uses $a(|x|+1)^k$ fair random bits for some natural numbers $a,k$, outputting the correct membership bit with probability at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of bit strings

For every input, all choice strings of the prescribed length lead to halting within that bound
